blocks.text: Multilevel inheritance in Python occurs when a class inherits from another drived class, creating a chain of inheritance similar to a family tree (Grandparent → Parent → Child). In this structure, the "grandchild" class has access to all methods and attributes from both its immediate parent and its grandparent (as shown in Figure 3.5).

blocks.alt: Multilevel inheritance: three boxes in a column, Grand Parent Class at the top, Parent Class in the middle and Child Class at the bottom; each lower class is joined to the one above by a line with a hollow arrowhead at the upper class.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.5: Multilevel Inheritance (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 3.5).

blocks.text: In this example, ElectricCar inherits from Car, which in turn inherits from Vehicle.

blocks.title: Class Activity
blocks.text: Create a Vehicle class and extend it with Car and Bike subclasses. Add unique methods to each subclass and demonstrate inheritance.
